title: Oscar and the Witness
premise: In the fog-bound coastal town of Marrow's Reach, coroner Beatrix Coldharbour has spent thirty years cataloguing the dead while keeping his own history buried. When a drowned woman washes up wearing clothes lifted from his closet, holding a page from a closed case file only he ever saw, Beatrix realizes someone is staging his old sins back to life. As the anniversary dinner of the town's founding approaches—the night his original crime was committed—Beatrix must unmask the killer, who is one of the witnesses he once protected, before the final toast is raised and the last name on his list becomes his own.
about_author: J. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade filing death certificates in a town of four hundred souls. They write mysteries about the quiet complicity of small communities, from a farmhouse that overlooks the sea.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Accounts
chapters.summary: Beatrix Coldharbour, POV. A drowned woman washes ashore wearing Beatrix's own missing cardigan and a watch engraved with a date he recognizes. He signs the death certificate with a hand that won't stay steady. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. He inventories his closet, confirms the theft, and burns nothing—though he wants to. Flashback seeds: a night in 1994 he has never spoken of. His housekeeper, Ivy, notices his sleeplessness. Emotional beat: the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: A File That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Detective Sergeant Nell Okafor, POV. The victim, Lena Voss, was a records clerk at the county archive. A photocopy of a sealed 1994 inquest page is found in her coat. Nell begins to wonder what her easygoing coroner is hiding. Emotional beat: suspicion as slow weather.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Committee
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Town elders press him to speak at the founding anniversary dinner. Among them: Aldous Greer, whose family built the town, and Father Ambrose, who was young in 1994. Beatrix accepts, trapped by his own good reputation. Emotional beat: the cage of respectability.

chapters.title: What Lena Knew
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Lena's flat reveals she was researching the 1994 drowning of a girl named Cass Merrow, ruled accidental. Lena's last phone call traced to a payphone outside the church. Emotional beat: the thrill of a thread pulled loose.

chapters.title: The Witness List
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. He reconstructs the 1994 inquest from memory: four witnesses, three still living in Marrow's Reach. One by one he visits them, and each claims innocence a shade too quickly. Emotional beat: old alliances curdling into mutual fear.

chapters.title: Second Body, Same Closet
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Witness Tom Pellow is found hanged in his boathouse, wearing Beatrix's missing scarf. The staging is precise—too precise. Nell confronts Beatrix with the pattern: the killer is dressing the dead in him. Emotional beat: cornered.

chapters.title: Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. He tells Nell a half-truth: he altered the 1994 inquest under pressure from Greer's father to protect the town's founding legacy. He omits what he himself saw. Nell believes him—mostly. Emotional beat: the relief and rot of a partial confession.

chapters.title: The Third Witness Runs
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Witness Marta Hale flees town before she can be questioned; her car is found at the ferry, keys in the ignition, a folded page of the case file on the seat. Someone is herding the witnesses like sheep. Emotional beat: mounting panic.

chapters.title: Ivy's Long Memory
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. His housekeeper Ivy reveals she was the inquest's stenographer and kept the original transcript hidden for thirty years. She gives it to him with a warning: the missing fourth witness was never named. Emotional beat: unexpected loyalty as a lifeline.

chapters.title: The Unnamed Fourth
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Reading the transcript, Beatrix confronts the truth he buried: the fourth witness was a child—himself. He saw Cass Merrow's death and let the adults bury it. Emotional beat: self-implication, the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Greer's Toast
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. At a rehearsal dinner, Aldous Greer gives a glib toast to the town's 'clean hands.' Nell notices Greer flinch when the 1994 date is mentioned—and notices someone photographing the room from the gallery. Emotional beat: performance and surveillance.

chapters.title: Marta Comes Back Dead
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Marta's body surfaces downcoast, dressed in Beatrix's old overcoat, a page pinned inside the lining. Three witnesses, three deaths, one costume each. The killer isn't punishing them—he's dressing Beatrix in his own guilt. Emotional beat: horror of recognition.

chapters.title: The Trap That Traps Its Maker
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Nell and Beatrix agree to stage a fake fourth witness statement naming the killer, seeded only to Greer. But the bait is ignored, and instead the archive copy of the 1994 file is stolen overnight. Emotional beat: the humbling of cleverness.

chapters.title: Father Ambrose's Ledger
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Dying Father Ambrose, in confession-adjacent honesty, hands Beatrix a ledger of the town's paid silences—including a monthly stipend to a family named Voss. Lena was Cass Merrow's half-sister. Emotional beat: grief reframing motive.

chapters.title: Not Vengeance, Accounting
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Nell theorizes the killer isn't Greer but someone making the town pay its debts in Beatrix's clothes—a witness turned executioner. She rechecks Lena's calls: the payphone outside the church, again and again, for months. Emotional beat: empathy for the hunter.

chapters.title: The Night of the Dinner
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Anniversary night. Two hundred guests, one toast, and Beatrix at the podium with the original transcript in his breast pocket. He sees the cardigan—his cardigan—on a figure at the back of the hall. Emotional beat: the trap closing from both ends.

chapters.title: The Fourth Witness Speaks
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. At the podium, instead of the rehearsed speech, Beatrix confesses publicly to what he saw in 1994 and what he buried. The room goes silent; Greer stands to object; the figure in the cardigan moves toward the doors. Emotional beat: liberation and terror at once.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Founders' Hall
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. The figure flees; Nell pursues through the kitchens and the old cellar where the town's records are kept. The killer is Ivy's estranged son, Rowan—Cass's childhood friend, who found the transcript while working for Lena. Emotional beat: pursuit edged with sorrow.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. Beatrix talks Rowan down at the sea wall: killing the witnesses only repeats what the town did to Cass. Rowan breaks, saying he wanted Beatrix to feel dressed in his own lie. He surrenders the final page. Emotional beat: mercy chosen over justice's easy arithmetic.

chapters.title: Reopening the Inquest
chapters.summary: Nell, POV. Weeks later: the 1994 inquest is formally reopened; Greer is charged with obstruction; Rowan pleads to manslaughter with Beatrix's testimony mitigating his sentence. Nell and Beatrix, wary allies now, file the amended report together. Emotional beat: justice arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix, POV. On the cliff above Cass Merrow's finally marked grave, Beatrix reads her name aloud at a small town gathering. He keeps his cardigan, washed clean, and begins writing a true account of 1994. Emotional beat: belonging earned through truth, not silence.
